cells.verb: keeping safe what the change left you
cells.place: in your sense of how things actually work
cells.ask: Trade one piece of what you understand for one piece of what someone else does, and see what comes back — the sense of what's fair tends to arrive on its own once the exchange is moving.
cells.core:
Something ended, and what it taught you about how things work has settled. You're not reciting the lesson and you're not guarding it — you're holding it, steady, the way you hold something that's finished cooking. It's quiet in there now. That quiet is earned, and you can feel the difference between earned quiet and just not talking about it.
It's yours. Which means it's also the kind of thing that can be shared without being spent.
cells.sheetLine: What the ending taught you has settled, and you're holding it well.

cells.tense: Future — bracing for the day it turns out to be wrong.
cells.verb: clutching what the change left you
cells.place: in your sense of how things actually work
cells.ask: Let one new thing pull at you — a person, a feeling, a moment — before you decide where it fits in what you already know. Stay with it long enough to feel it without becoming it. What comes back is a kept understanding that can still move: endings honored, and the next change trusted instead of guarded against.
cells.core:
You paid for what you know about how things work, and now you're guarding it like it could be taken. Everything that comes in gets filed into the shape you already have, fast, before it can unsettle anything. Somewhere ahead is a version where the understanding fails you, and you're bracing for it now by not letting anything near it.
What was meant to be kept has become something you're defending. It's getting smaller the harder you hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the lesson so hard nothing new can reach it.

cells.tense: Past — still at the door of something already over.
cells.verb: letting slip what the change left you
cells.place: in your sense of how things actually work
cells.ask: Pick one thing that ending taught you — just one — and move on it this week, in one direction, and stand behind that direction when it gets pushed. Not to make yourself hold the lesson; moving on it is what makes it stay. What comes back is the ending finally honored, and some trust that what follows it can be kept.
cells.core:
You went through it. You could tell someone exactly how it worked, where it broke, what was underneath. But you're not keeping any of that — it leaks out, and you find yourself back at the same spot learning the same thing again. The understanding comes; it just doesn't stay put.
The change happened. What it produced never got set down anywhere safe. So you're still standing at a door that's already closed.
cells.sheetLine: You understood it. You just never kept what you understood.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you're keeping it and calling it obvious.
cells.verb: holding what the change left you
cells.place: in your sense of how things actually work
cells.ask: Say the rule you're living by out loud, plainly, once, as something you chose to keep — not as the way things are. What comes back is a clarity that other people can actually use, because it's got an owner now: the ending claimed, and the next change trusted.
cells.core:
You're already running on a settled understanding of how things work. It steers what you let in, what you dismiss, what you build on. It got settled by something that ended, and you kept it, carefully. But you'd describe it as just seeing clearly — "that's how it is" — as if the understanding weren't something you're holding.
The keeping is doing its work. Nobody, including you, is saying who's keeping it.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding a hard-won understanding and calling it common sense.
